events.title: London Lock Hospital opens for venereal disease patients
events.description: The Lock Hospital at Hyde Park Corner opened as the first hospital in Britain dedicated to treating venereal disease. It later added a chapel and an asylum for women.
events.html: The Lock Hospital at Hyde Park Corner opened as the first hospital in Britain dedicated to treating venereal disease. It later added a chapel and an asylum for women.

events.title: US House passes the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery
events.description: After intense lobbying by President Lincoln, the House of Representatives approved the amendment by 119 votes to 56. Ratified in December 1865, it ended slavery throughout the United States.
events.html: After intense lobbying by President Lincoln, the House of Representatives approved the amendment by 119 votes to 56. Ratified in December 1865, it ended slavery throughout the United States.

events.title: Germany announces unrestricted submarine warfare
events.description: Germany told the United States its U-boats would sink without warning any ship in the war zone from the next day. The decision led to the break in relations and, in April, to America's declaration of war.
events.html: Germany told the United States its U-boats would sink without warning any ship in the war zone from the next day. The decision led to the break in relations and, in April, to America's declaration of war.

events.title: Police clash with strikers in Glasgow's George Square
events.description: A rally for a 40-hour week ended in violence between police and workers in George Square. Fearing revolution, the government sent troops and tanks into Glasgow.
events.html: A rally for a 40-hour week ended in violence between police and workers in George Square. Fearing revolution, the government sent troops and tanks into Glasgow.

events.title: First monthly Social Security cheque is issued
events.description: Ida May Fuller, a retired legal secretary from Vermont, received cheque number 00-000-001 for 22.54 dollars. She lived to 100 and collected about 22,000 dollars in benefits.
events.html: Ida May Fuller, a retired legal secretary from Vermont, received cheque number 00-000-001 for 22.54 dollars. She lived to 100 and collected about 22,000 dollars in benefits.

events.title: Private Eddie Slovik executed for desertion
events.description: Slovik was shot by firing squad in eastern France, the only American soldier executed for desertion since the Civil War. Of many soldiers sentenced to death for the offence, he alone was put to death.
events.html: Slovik was shot by firing squad in eastern France, the only American soldier executed for desertion since the Civil War. Of many soldiers sentenced to death for the offence, he alone was put to death.

events.title: Explorer 1, America's first satellite, is launched
events.description: A Jupiter-C rocket put Explorer 1 into orbit from Cape Canaveral, four months after Sputnik. Its Geiger counter detected the Van Allen radiation belts around the Earth.
events.html: A Jupiter-C rocket put Explorer 1 into orbit from Cape Canaveral, four months after Sputnik. Its Geiger counter detected the Van Allen radiation belts around the Earth.

events.title: Ham the chimpanzee flies into space
events.description: Ham flew a suborbital flight on Mercury-Redstone 2, performing simple tasks in response to lights. His safe return cleared the way for Alan Shepard's flight that May.
events.html: Ham flew a suborbital flight on Mercury-Redstone 2, performing simple tasks in response to lights. His safe return cleared the way for Alan Shepard's flight that May.

events.title: Apollo 14 launches for the Moon
events.description: Alan Shepard, Stuart Roosa and Edgar Mitchell lifted off from Kennedy Space Center. Landing at Fra Mauro on 5 February, Shepard famously hit two golf balls on the lunar surface.
events.html: Alan Shepard, Stuart Roosa and Edgar Mitchell lifted off from Kennedy Space Center. Landing at Fra Mauro on 5 February, Shepard famously hit two golf balls on the lunar surface.

events.title: McDonald's opens in Moscow
events.description: The first McDonald's in the Soviet Union opened on Pushkin Square, serving about 30,000 people on its first day. Queues stretched for hours as the Cold War drew to a close.
events.html: The first McDonald's in the Soviet Union opened on Pushkin Square, serving about 30,000 people on its first day. Queues stretched for hours as the Cold War drew to a close.
